paragraphs: Cornwall Council runs its own fostering service for Cornwall and the Isles of Scilly and says it has a real shortage of foster carers: at any one time around 30 children and young people in Cornwall need a place to call home. Children may also live with independent agencies such as those listed on this page.

Enquiries to the council go through Fostering South West, a regional recruitment hub covering the peninsula that answers first questions and then puts prospective carers in touch with their own council. The council has previously appealed in particular for carers for children aged 10 and over, and short breaks are one of the types of fostering it offers.

To foster for the council you need to be over 21 and have your own home, which can be rented or owned. The council says single people, people living in flats and LGBTQ+ people can all foster. Carers receive financial allowances, training and ongoing support, including from a specialist fostering support team.
Before deciding, compare what the council offers with two or three of the agencies below, and ask each about pay, training and support where you live in Cornwall.

sources.title: New fostering recruitment hub aims to create more loving homes for vulnerable children in Cornwall (Cornwall Council)
